title: When I Get Frustrated — Social Story (Allison Fors)

unmappedSkills.description: Identify and use calming strategies (deep breaths, counting to 10, walking away, squeezing a stress ball) when experiencing strong emotions like frustration
Engage with first-person social stories that normalize emotions, describe body signals, and model coping strategies

characters: diverse cartoon children (multiple skin tones, hair types)

printFormat.colorRequirement: color optional — B&W version included for coloring
printFormat.foldInstructions: included — single page folds into 8-page mini book

gaps: one-page-mini-book: single letter-size page with 8-panel grid that folds (fold all lines → fold in half → cut center dotted line → fold lengthwise → push in ends → fold closed) into an 8-page mini book. Requires precise panel placement so pages read in correct order after folding.

social-narrative: first-person story format with illustration + text per page, following a pattern: normalize the emotion → describe body signals → state the goal → list coping strategies → end with positive affirmation + open-ended question

components.name: Fold Instructions Page
components.description: Step-by-step visual guide for folding: (1) fold along all lines, (2) fold in half and cut center dotted line, (3) open and fold lengthwise, (4) push in both ends, (5) fold and close. Shows finished mini book photo.
designPatterns: Visual fold instructions with numbered steps and diagrams
Photo of finished product sets expectations

components.name: Mini Book — Color Version (8 panels on one page)
components.description: Single page, 4x2 grid. When folded, creates an 8-page story: Cover ('When I Get Frustrated... Social Story') → Page 2 (frustration is normal, body signals: tight body, hot face, fast heart) → Page 3 (I want to make safe choices, here are things I can do) → Page 4 (count to 10 slowly with fingers) → Page 5 (walk away, ask for a break, say 'I need space') → Page 6 (squeeze something soft — pillow, stuffed animal, stress ball) → Page 7 (take deep breaths to calm down) → Page 8 (positive affirmation + open question: 'What else helps me when I get frustrated?'). Full color with diverse cartoon children.
designPatterns: Social narrative structure: normalize → describe → model strategies → affirm
First-person voice: 'I can...' statements empower the child
One strategy per page: no overwhelm
Diverse representation: different children on each page (skin tones, hair, clothing)
Open-ended question on last page: invites personalization and conversation
Illustration-dominant: large character art, short text

components.name: Mini Book — B&W Version
components.description: Same content and layout as color version but in black and white line art. Doubles as a coloring activity.
designPatterns: Dual-version approach: color for quick use, B&W for engagement (coloring while reading)
No-print option noted: can view on device

components.name: Large B&W Version (individual pages)
components.description: Same story broken into individual full-page spreads (2 panels per page). Larger text and illustrations for younger readers or group reading.
designPatterns: Size differentiation: mini book for individual, large pages for group/circle time

notes: First non-academic reference. This is SEL (social-emotional learning) — a subject Homa's taxonomy has some coverage on (Emotional Literacy domain) but no material recipes for. The mini-book format is fascinating: one page becomes an 8-page book via folding. That's a printable format Homa could own — generate personalized social stories as single-page foldable mini books. The social narrative structure (normalize → body signals → coping strategies → affirmation) is a therapeutic format used widely in special ed and early childhood. Sid dropping this alongside the Adapting for Autism CVC worksheets suggests interest in inclusive/therapeutic educational formats, not just academic drill.
